units.translation: wielding his well-rounded shield, i.e. turning it, as in the same place 542: in the bronze-wrought shield he moved the Sphinx, the eater of raw flesh, fastened with bolts.
For it is better for us to perish or to enjoy honors, i.e. to have the enjoyment of honors.
whom Zeus the all-powerful and Ares, the guardian of the gods, protect.
both gods and mortals who dwell in the city of Pallas.
so may the city be well governed.
they inhabit the seat of Asia.
who dwell near the city of Caucasus. This has been restored from the lemma of the scholium and the copies for νέμουσι [they dwell].
in the manner of a newly married bride.

a newborn might learn from men, a corrupt reading, which Hermann plausibly corrected to καὶ παῖς νεόγονος ἂν μάθοι [and a newborn child might learn], as the meter of the antistrophic verse 1174 requires.
Wunder proposed νεοδρόπους [freshly plucked] (which form the meter requires in the same place, line 354): but there is no need. Theocritus and others used νεόδρεπτος [freshly plucked].
newly suckled. An adjective formed from θηλή [nipple] like εὔθηλος [with good nipples].

It is the law that the murderer be speechless until the blood of a newly suckled victim has been shed upon him by a man who purifies from bloodshed. In M it is καθαιμάξουσιν οθήλου [they will stain with blood of...], with ζήτει [look for] written in the margin. Turnebus corrected it.

new, strange. ("κότος [disposition] properly means nature: hence ἀλλόκοτος [of another kind], νεόκοτος [of new kind]. But the common meaning is anger. Aeschylus loves compounds with κότος [disposition]." Blomfield in the Glossary on Sept. 804.)
I cry out strange, terrible, great griefs, where I added νεόκοτα [strange] by conjecture, since no more suitable word for this passage could be found.
Similarly νέον ἄχος μέγα [new great grief] is said at Ag. 1101 and Sept. 803: τί δ᾽ ἐστὶ πρᾶγος νεόκοτον πόλει πάλιν; [What is this strange matter for the city again?]

Improperly, newly united. Ch. 344 νεοκρᾶτα φίλον κομίσειεν [may he bring a newly mixed friend], which the scholiast explains as τὸν νεωστί συγκραθέντα ἡμῖν [the one newly mixed with us]. On the acute accent see Choerob. vol. 1 p. 49, 8. 141, 18. 350, 22.
may he bring a newly mixed friend
the one newly mixed with us
For all the youth has now perished.
May the Lycian god be gracious to all the youth. See Thes. vol. 5 p. 1431.
a newly founded city. A word not found anywhere else.
newly drawn, an adjective with a long penultimate syllable formed from ῥύομαι [I draw].
